acceptance: A timed-out mutation can be reconciled without reading the whole item: the response or a follow-up read by operation ID says whether it applied.
Retrying the same `context_append` with the same operation ID does not append twice.
The cause of the slow calls under load (Git fetch or push to the state branch, lock contention, or other) is identified and written in this item.
description:
Reliability gap, three occurrences on 2026-11-12 under heavy host load (load average 8-37, swap above 90%): `list_items(text="duckdb 2")`, one `update_item(context_append=...)`, and a second `update_item` inside a scripted sequence each failed with `Request timeout after 30000ms ... the request outcome is unknown`. Both writes had in fact landed, found by re-reading the item. A caller that retried blindly would have appended the note twice; a caller that assumed failure would have lost track of a write.

Expected: either mutations finish within the client timeout under load, or the timeout response carries the operation ID so the caller can reconcile as it does for `E_UNKNOWN`, and `context_append` retries are idempotent for the same operation ID.

Guardrails: a change in the tractable product or in the client timeout configuration, not a BenchBox wrapper. Do not raise the timeout so far that a hung server blocks a session.
